newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan says plans to tap capital markets further.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says plans to tap capital markets further.

text.p: Pakistan intends to tap tap the capital markets further in the next (July/June) fiscal year and is considering issuing Samurai bonds, a Ministry of Finance official told Reuters in an interview on Monday.

"We do plan to access capital markets more often next year...This year we tried out the idea of going with a Samurai bond. Unfortunately we didn't get the time to do that, but next year we might do that," Javed Ahmed Noel said.
He added Pakistan may also issue a sterling bond next year.
He said some of Pakistan's external debt was denominated in yen and borrowed when the yen was trading at around 250 to the U.S. dollar.
It stands at around 125 yen now, effectively making the loans twice as expensive to repay in dollars.
For this reason, "We'd like to go for Samurais more often," Noel added.
Turning to the economy, Noel said Pakistan was expecting 1996/97 fiscal year Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth of around six percent.
"But it may be slightly less because we haven't as good a cotton crop as we'd expected and our wheat harvest is also expected to be slightly below the normal this year," he added.
Noel said Pakistan's budget deficit as a percentage of GDP was likely to "be above five percent" for fiscal 1996/97. This compares with an original 1996/97 budget estimate of four percent.
Officials of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would be visiting Pakistan in late June or early July for further discussions on a new Extended Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF), he said.
A previous US$1.2 billion ESAF fell through when the IMF concluded that Pakistan's previous caretaker government could not meet its conditions.
"The new ESAF package should be in place by September," Noel said.
Noel is in Singapore as part of the roadshow for investors for a U.S. dollar, three-year floating rate note eurobond which should be launched later this month.
Officials from lead manager ANZ Merchant Bank said the offering will be for U.S.$100 million or, depending on demand, possibly more.
Present price talk is at around 375 to 425 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
The roadshow will be in Tokyo on Tuesday, Seoul on Wednesday and London on Friday.
